Lessons ledger#

Rows are sorted by ledger ID, including dropped and superseded evidence. Scope records the source claim; it does not certify promotion to a general lesson. The disposition records editorial placement, not publication approval of an archived original. Source links resolve to bibliography metadata, including held-back notices.

L-1001#

2006; Seattle; ONE/Northwest; S009.

Scope: specific. Confidence: observed. Status: active.

Topic: conference-data-table. Disposition: placed: conference-data-table.

Plone Conference 2006 ran three conference days in late October 2006 with about 350 attendees from 35 U.S. states and 20 countries, preceded by two days of training for over 110 students and followed by a two-day sprint with about 50 participants.

Locator: Overview.

L-1002#

2006; Seattle; ONE/Northwest; S086.

Scope: specific. Confidence: observed. Status: active.

Topic: conference-data-table. Disposition: placed: conference-data-table.

The 2006 evaluation (about 140 respondents) profiled the audience: business 41%, technology consulting 34%, nonprofit 31%, education 26%, government 16% and scientific research 11% (multiple answers allowed); about 22% had used Plone little or not at all before attending.

Locator: Sector and prior-knowledge questions.

L-1003#

2006; Seattle; ONE/Northwest; S008.

Scope: specific. Confidence: observed. Status: active.

Topic: handover-contract. Disposition: placed: handover-contract#case-notes.

The 2006 organizers published their whole evaluation on one public page: the pre-conference survey, the aggregated post-conference survey, the open-ended attendee comments, the detailed budget and a narrative lessons document addressed to future organizers.

Locator: Evaluation index.

L-1004#

2006; Seattle; ONE/Northwest; S009.

Scope: specific. Confidence: observed. Status: active.

Topic: handover-contract. Disposition: placed: handover-contract#case-notes.

The lessons document was written by the lead organizer after the event, with input from the co-organizer, the host's finance staff and several community advisers, and states its purpose as passing the host organization's experience to future Plone event organizers.

Locator: Purpose of this document; Overview.

L-1005#

2006; Seattle; ONE/Northwest; S009.

Scope: specific. Confidence: observed. Status: active.

Topic: handover-contract. Disposition: placed: handover-contract#case-notes.

Per-session evaluation results were kept private but offered to future conference organizers on request; no public record shows whether that hand-over happened.

Locator: Things We Might Do Differently Next Time.

L-1006#

2006; Seattle; ONE/Northwest; S009.

Scope: specific. Confidence: observed. Status: active.

Topic: team-and-governance. Disposition: placed: team-and-governance#case-notes.

Two staff members of the host organization ran the conference as a project, backed by a colleague handling the money, another handling logistics, and staff of a partner nonprofit during conference week; organizing took over 350 staff hours.

Locator: Overview; Budget; Thanks.

L-1007#

2006; Seattle; ONE/Northwest; S009.

Scope: general. Confidence: observed. Status: active.

Topic: stakeholder-map. Disposition: placed: stakeholder-map#principles-and-general-lessons.

The organizers relied on a small circle of long-standing community leaders as advisers on strategic and tactical questions, and recommend that future organizers tap the same kind of experience.

Locator: Thanks and Acknowledgements.

L-1008#

2006; Seattle; ONE/Northwest; S009.

Scope: specific. Confidence: observed. Status: active.

Topic: volunteers-and-roles. Disposition: placed: volunteers-and-roles#case-notes.

Members of the local user community lent projectors, extension cords and other equipment, and a professional designer from the community repeatedly rescued deadlines in the last days before the event.

Locator: Thanks and Acknowledgements.

L-1009#

2006; Seattle; ONE/Northwest; S009.

Scope: general. Confidence: observed. Status: active.

Topic: master-timeline. Disposition: placed: master-timeline#principles-and-general-lessons.

We recommend starting the conference planning process six months in advance.

Locator: Master Timeline.

Scope: specific. Confidence: observed. Status: active.

Topic: ticketing-and-registration. Disposition: placed: ticketing-and-registration#case-notes.

Value for money averaged 4.30 on 20 ratings, with four 3s that carry no stated reason. The three self-paid respondents were at least as satisfied as average, hotel-cost critics still rated value highly, and nobody mentioned the ticket price.

Locator: Ratings at a glance; Findings: Value for money.

L-6037#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: ticketing-and-registration. Disposition: placed: ticketing-and-registration#case-notes.

The analyst first read the low value scores as venue-cost driven, and the data contradicted it. Price perception is a blind spot, not a confirmed problem; ask about it directly in the next survey instead of guessing.

Locator: Interpretation, point 5 (analyst's reading).

L-6038#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: observed. Status: active.

Topic: programme-portfolio. Disposition: placed: programme-portfolio#case-notes.

Of 18 respondents profiling why they attend, 9 come technology-first but appreciate context and business talks, 6 come equally for both, 2 want deep technical content only and 1 came mainly for business and strategy.

Locator: Findings: Content balance.

L-6039#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: keynotes-and-invited-talks. Disposition: placed: keynotes-and-invited-talks#case-notes.

The content mix drew an unresolved disagreement. One respondent asked to keep mind-broadening keynotes, another to stop keynotes unrelated to IT, and a third to stop talks involving AI; the majority profile wants the mix.

Locator: Findings: Content balance; Interpretation, point 6.

L-6040#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: programme-portfolio. Disposition: placed: programme-portfolio#case-notes.

Opinion, not a data finding — the analyst recommends keeping the broadening keynotes and practical AI content, making the technical core unmistakably strong, and treating AI as one topic among many rather than the conference's identity.

Locator: Interpretation, point 6, last sentences (explicitly the analyst's opinion).

L-6041#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: observed. Status: active.

Topic: defining-success. Disposition: placed: defining-success#case-notes.

Asked about attending the 2027 conference in Bucharest, 16 respondents said yes, 2 perhaps and 3 probably not.

Locator: Ratings at a glance (paragraph below the table).

L-6042#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: defining-success. Disposition: placed: defining-success#case-notes.

Return intent is survivor-biased. The three respondents who skipped the why-attend profile are exactly the three probably-nots for 2027, and one of them rated the conference 5 overall, so intent measures more than satisfaction and the happiest-looking profile excludes those drifting away.

Locator: Interpretation, point 6 (analyst's reading).

L-6043#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: print-and-merch. Disposition: placed: print-and-merch#case-notes.

Two respondents independently asked for badges printed on both sides instead of one.

Locator: Findings: Small operational wishes; Consolidated stop list.

L-6044#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: speakers-and-speaker-care. Disposition: placed: speakers-and-speaker-care#how-to.

A respondent asked for speaker introductions that include some background, not just a name.

Locator: Findings: Small operational wishes.

L-6045#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: speakers-and-speaker-care. Disposition: placed: speakers-and-speaker-care#how-to.

A respondent asked for a feedback form for each talk, so speakers get feedback on their own session.

Locator: Findings: Small operational wishes.

L-6046#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: scheduling. Disposition: placed: scheduling#case-notes.

A respondent asked for 3-minute lightning talks instead of 5. This converges with the Arnhem 2012 advice that lightning talks work better at 3 to 4 minutes (L-2099).

Locator: Findings: Small operational wishes; cross-note to L-2099.

L-6047#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: scheduling. Disposition: placed: scheduling#case-notes.

Respondents' keep-doing list included the two-room parallel structure, the pace, the open spaces and the buffers between talks.

Locator: Consolidated start / keep / stop — Keep.

L-6048#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: ticketing-and-registration. Disposition: placed: ticketing-and-registration#case-notes.

A respondent asked that the next edition open its website, advertising and ticket sales earlier.

Locator: Findings: Small operational wishes.

L-6049#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: social-events-and-party. Disposition: placed: social-events-and-party#case-notes.

A respondent asked specifically for organized evening socializing on the training and sprint days, which sit outside the main conference evenings and the party.

Locator: Findings: Small operational wishes; Consolidated start list.

L-6050#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: marketing-and-outreach. Disposition: placed: marketing-and-outreach#case-notes.

A respondent asked to invite students and younger developers to the training days. This corroborates the planned 2026 university and audience outreach that was dropped before execution (L-5036, L-5037).

Locator: Findings: Small operational wishes; cross-note to L-5036 and L-5037.

L-6051#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: print-and-merch. Disposition: placed: print-and-merch#case-notes.

A respondent asked for t-shirts with less conspicuous lettering and a more artistic design that gets worn for years, naming the Seattle and Budapest shirts as the ones they wore most. Belongs in the 2027 print brief.

Locator: Findings: T-shirts drew two specific criticisms.

L-6052#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: print-and-merch. Disposition: placed: print-and-merch#case-notes.

A respondent listed female-cut t-shirts under stop-doing; the analysis records no reason. The 2027 print brief should weigh this single request against offering more than one fit.

Locator: Findings: T-shirts drew two specific criticisms; Consolidated stop list.

L-6053#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: programme-portfolio. Disposition: placed: programme-portfolio#case-notes.

One respondent suggested a co-located PyCon day as a start item.

Locator: Consolidated start / keep / stop — Start (one vote).

L-6054#

2026; Maastricht; Plone Conference 2026 organizing team; S110.

Scope: specific. Confidence: reported. Status: active.

Topic: sprints. Disposition: dropped: too vague to act on; the analysis records a single unexplained stop item without context.

One respondent's stop-doing item was spreading developer efforts.

Locator: Consolidated start / keep / stop — Stop.
